question.text: A car accelerates from rest of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The energy spent in this process is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The energy required to accelerate the car from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>u</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mi>E</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is _____.

solution.text:
The kinetic energy of a moving particle is given by

E=12mu2   ...(1)

When the final velocity of the particle becomes twice the initial velocity, the kinetic energy of the particle can be written as

nE=12m(2u)2-u2= 12m3u2   ...2

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of n.

nEE=12m3u212mu2⇒n=3
